# Native stock Reference, Split and Waveshaper

ML Split adapts the three-way phase-alignment topology from ChowDSP's CrossoverFilter (chowdsp_utils revision ffc70ba399f9afaeefb996eb14e55a1d487270b8), staged through ChowMultiTool revision fed56c01a14503d6416e6cd1036e6455f646fd8a. Upstream: https://github.com/Chowdhury-DSP/chowdsp_utils ; modules/dsp/chowdsp_filters/Other/chowdsp_CrossoverFilter.h. Copyright Jatin Chowdhury / Chowdhury DSP, GPLv3. The repository GPL licence is in LICENSE. The adaptation uses native Rust TPT Butterworth sections in a fourth-order Linkwitz-Riley crossover, with the upper crossover's allpass sum applied to the low band. Frequency, gain and band-selection changes are smoothed. The summed magnitude is flat; phase is not identical to unfiltered input. No JUCE dependency or plugin binary is embedded.

ML Waveshaper uses an original native piecewise-linear nine-point transfer curve and fixed 4x Blackman-window FIR oversampling (129 taps in each direction). The staged ChowMultiTool spline/ADAA implementation was reviewed; its JUCE shell, async preparation and spline/ADAA code are not used. The native design supports parameter automation, shared editor gestures/undo and fixed 32-sample host compensation. Its aligned dry path is exact at Mix 0%; the linear wet path is low-pass filtered near Nyquist. Oversampling reduces aliasing, not a guarantee of eliminating it. DC removal is a 10 Hz first-order high-pass after shaping.

ML Reference uses the existing os-engine audio decoder, os-dsp table/windowed-sinc resampler and ebur128 0.1.11 (MIT, notices already included). No proprietary presets, reference recordings or third-party reference-plugin code are bundled. File decoding and buffer destruction run on a worker; ownership transfers with atomic pointers. Audio owns its active Track; the worker owns pending/retired slots after exchange. Replacement waits for the A/B fade and retired-slot reclaim. Plugin teardown joins the worker. Linked paths persist; audio files are not embedded. Files are limited to 256 MiB compressed and 20 minutes decoded at 8-192 kHz; decoding uses the existing whole-file loader.

Level matching uses EBU momentary loudness for the first three seconds, then short-term loudness, requiring at least 400 ms of non-silent measurements. Matching freezes during reference audition. Reference gain is capped against decoded sample peaks at -1 dBFS; this is not a true-peak limiter. Offline processing returns the live input unchanged, verified through the actual CLAP host render-mode extension. A/B listening is transient and returns to Your mix on reopen/load.

All three are linked stock effects and use the existing ML frame, parameter state/automation and visibility setting. Split is stereo, not an auxiliary multi-output effect: the host does not yet route arbitrary effect outputs, so separate bands use three parallel instances. Tests cover actual CLAP state/latency/offline rendering, DSP behavior, callback allocation/free detection, parameter editing and editor renders. Hands-on listening and platform-native Mac/Linux builds require separate verification.
